clue.text: Angels around one put in his crib sculpted with love

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are wrapped around the single numeral, so it ends up inside them
something sculpted has been reshaped, so these letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A nativity scene: angels gather round a baby laid in his crib, lovingly carved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put' simply joins. The phrase comes from George Eliot's poem and the Monty Python dead-parrot sketch, where the parrot has 'joined the choir invisible': the theme is musicians who have died.
explanation.definitionFit: The unseen heavenly host of the dead is poetically described as a chorus of angels singing out of sight.

clue.text: Made up hoax about politician's pay increase

indicators.note: the word for a hoax goes around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: a cod is a hoax or joke, as in a cod accent
MP is a Member of Parliament, the 's just a possessive
a rise is the British word for a raise in salary

explanation.surface: A scandal: a spoof story about an MP's salary hike.
explanation.walkthrough: Cod is British slang for a hoax or fake, and a rise is the British word for a pay raise.
explanation.definitionFit: Something comprised of parts is constituted or formed by them, so it is made up of them.

clue.text: Initially obsequious Shakespearean received in court

definitions.text: Initially obsequious Shakespearean received in court

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the opening letter of each of the following five words

explanation.surface: A fawning character from Shakespeare welcomed at a royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of the five words after 'Initially' spell the answer, and the whole clue describes him: the foppish, fawning courtier in Hamlet who referees the final duel.
explanation.definitionFit: This minor Hamlet character is a sycophantic courtier, exactly the obsequious figure of Shakespeare met at court.

clue.text: Short way to achieve total victory

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: a route is a way to go somewhere

explanation.surface: Advice on the quickest path to crushing an opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts the last letter off ROUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is an overwhelming defeat of an enemy, so for the winner it is a complete triumph.

clue.text: See 1
This clue and why they say it could go with 14

parts.note: this clue is number 4, written in Roman numerals as IV

indicators.note: they say signals that the word is to be taken by how it is pronounced

parts.note: the word why is pronounced like the letter Y

explanation.surface: A puzzling self-referential clue about pairing with another entry.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue refers to its own number: 4 is IV in Roman numerals. 'they say' turns 'why' into the letter Y. 14-across's answer is the evergreen paired with this one in the Christmas carol.
explanation.definitionFit: The carol about the two evergreens pairs this climbing plant with the prickly red-berried shrub at 14.

clue.text: Sixes fly on both sides to make things exciting

parts.note: six is VI in Roman numerals, so two sixes give VI twice

indicators.note: on both sides asks for the letters at each edge of the word fly

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: sixes flying off the bat from both ends liven up a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Two VIs (sixes) are followed by the outside letters of 'fly'.
explanation.definitionFit: To vivify is to enliven or animate, giving life and excitement to something dull.

clue.text: Sickly sweet child on board a vehicle during function

indicators.note: during means the following pieces sit inside the word for a function

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function

indicators.note: on board means one piece is carried inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A cloying scene of a child riding in a car on the way to some event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' looks like a social event but is the trigonometric one.
explanation.definitionFit: Saccharine means excessively sentimental or cloying, the way an artificial sweetener is too sugary.

clue.text: Cook to get hot right inside

indicators.note: inside means the abbreviation is placed within the other word

parts.note: to boil is to get very hot

explanation.surface: Kitchen advice: to cook, get the heat right up.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) goes inside BOIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To broil is to cook meat by direct heat, grilling it; a standard American cooking verb.

clue.text: Lots of words sound as if spelt out backwards

indicators.note: spelt out backwards means the little word is reversed and its letters said by their names

parts.note: the word as read backwards gives the two letters S then A

explanation.surface: A wordy observation about how something reads when reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' read backwards is SA, and naming those letters one by one gives 'ess-ay'. 'sound' and 'if' join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A composition of many sentences on one subject is a substantial piece of prose, literally lots of words.

clue.text: Happy to include copper as a heavy metal

indicators.note: to include means the first word takes the symbol inside itself

parts.note: merry means happy
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A cheerful remark about copper counting as a heavy metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy metal' looks like a music genre, which fits the theme of dead musicians (Freddie of Queen), but here it is the dense liquid element.
explanation.definitionFit: Quicksilver is a dense metallic element, liquid at room temperature, and classed among the heavy metals.

clue.text: Mean to run away from, having won

indicators.note: to run away from means these letters leave the longer word

parts.note: victorious means having won
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A spiteful winner who runs off after the match.
explanation.walkthrough: TO and R (run) are taken out of VICTORIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruel, nasty and spiteful behaviour can be called mean, a close synonym for savage malice.

clue.text: Abandoning diet, Marlene becomes well-endowed

indicators.note: abandoning means the word diet is dropped from the surname

parts.note: Marlene Dietrich was the German-born Hollywood star

explanation.surface: A film star gives up her diet and becomes buxom.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove DIET from the start of DIETRICH. 'Well-endowed' suggests a figure, but here means wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well endowed with money or resources is wealthy, an affluent person with plenty of funds.

clue.text: Get down quickly and run back

indicators.note: back means the word for run is read in reverse

parts.note: to flow is to run, as liquid does

explanation.surface: An instruction to drop quickly and then hurry back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get down' sounds like ducking or crouching, but it means swallowing food.
explanation.definitionFit: To wolf food is to gulp or devour it greedily, getting it down in a hurry.

clue.text: Sign of submariner surfacing

indicators.note: in a down clue surfacing means coming upwards, so the name is read from the bottom

parts.note: Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's novel

explanation.surface: A sign that a submarine crewman is coming up.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain NEMO, Jules Verne's submarine captain, reads upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent or augury is a sign foretelling what is to come.

clue.text: Quite unoriginal decoration?

indicators.note: unoriginal is read as losing the original, that is the first, letter

parts.note: quite can mean wholly, as in quite finished

explanation.surface: A sniffy verdict that some ornament is completely clichéd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unoriginal' removes the first letter from WHOLLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprigs of the red-berried evergreen are a traditional Christmas decoration hung around the home.

clue.text: I've built with a permit — it's essential

indicators.note: built means the letters are put together in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: A homeowner insists that having planning permission was vital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built' rearranges IVE plus APERMIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absolutely necessary or vital is described as an imperative, or as essential.

clue.text: Guitarist from Turkey opening season

indicators.note: opening means the letters prise apart the season and sit inside it

parts.note: summer is a season
TR is the international code for Turkey

explanation.surface: A guitarist from Turkey launches the festival season.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also the surname of Joe, the late Clash frontman, one of the theme's dead musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sweeps the strings of a guitar plays it, and the frontman of The Clash bore that name.

clue.text: Foreign film flew by

definitions.meaning: Akira Kurosawa's 1985 Japanese epic based on King Lear
to fly is to move fast, as in time flew by

explanation.surface: Time spent at an overseas movie passed quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Kurosawa's King Lear epic bears this title, and sped or hurried can be past-tense synonyms for flew.

clue.text: Charge about North of Wales maybe?

indicators.note: about means the word for a charge goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: a price is a charge

explanation.surface: A query about a fee in the north of Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North of Wales' looks like a place, but the definition is the blank before 'of Wales', the heir's title. The theme musician of Purple Rain fame bore the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The heir to the British throne holds the title that fits the gap before of Wales.

clue.text: FA's incomplete line-up

definitions.note: short for sweet Fanny Adams, British slang for nothing at all

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the letters are read from the bottom
incomplete means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The Football Association's team sheet is unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' cuts LINE to LIN, and 'up' reverses it. 'FA' is British slang for nothing (sweet Fanny Adams), not the Football Association.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet Fanny Adams means nothing whatsoever, and a score of zero in football is the same idea.

clue.text: Share open broadcast or they'll relay performance privately

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to share and air a show, or else listen to it in private.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges SHAREOPEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Headphones worn over or in the ears deliver music or a show to one listener alone.

clue.text: What's afoot? The girl's in love? Just the opposite!

indicators.note: the reverse of the girl being in love, so love goes inside the word for the girl

parts.note: the girl's is read as the girl is, she
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A gossip asks what is going on: is the girl in love? No, the reverse!
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' would put SHE inside O; 'Just the opposite' flips that, putting O inside SHE. 'What's afoot' means what's happening, but literally what goes on a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear is literally worn on the foot, which makes it the thing that is afoot.

clue.text: Part of Colorado Springs from garden, Versailles

indicators.note: springs from means the letters emerge from within these words

explanation.surface: A town in Colorado named after a garden at Versailles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colorado Springs' looks like the city, but 'Springs from' signals letters inside 'garden, Versailles'. The answer is also the surname of the late country singer John.
explanation.definitionFit: The state capital, the Mile High City, is a city that forms part of Colorado.

clue.text: Get name in credit or he could make things wicked for you

definitions.text: he could make things wicked for you

indicators.note: in means the word for a name sits inside the abbreviation for credit

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
a handle is slang for a name, as in a CB radio handle

explanation.surface: A warning that someone might ruin your credit rating if they get your name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' looks like evil, but means fitted with wicks: the trade is candle-making. The thriller writer Raymond shares the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional maker and seller of candles supplies items that have wicks.

clue.text: Make better after loud shock

indicators.note: after places the word for make better following the musical abbreviation

parts.note: F stands for forte, loud in music
to right something is to correct it or make it better

explanation.surface: Someone tries to improve things after a loud jolt.
explanation.walkthrough: F is forte, the musical direction for loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden scare or alarm is a shock to the nerves.

clue.text: City holds a place for Kiwis' opera star

indicators.note: holds means the city's letters go around the others

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
Kiwis are New Zealanders, and NZ is their country

explanation.surface: Los Angeles finds room for a New Zealand opera singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Mario was an American tenor and film star of the 1950s; Kiwis are New Zealanders.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hollywood tenor Mario was a famous operatic singer of the 1950s screen.

clue.text: Musical player regularly in charge

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word player

explanation.surface: A performer who is always the one in command.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'player' give LYR, then IC (in charge).
explanation.definitionFit: Lyric as an adjective describes poetry or singing meant to be set to music, so it means musical.

clue.text: Drain fluid to the very bottom

indicators.note: fluid means flowing and changeable, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Draining liquid right down to the bottom of a tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluid' rearranges DRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest point of anything, such as fortunes or a heavenly body's path, is its nadir.

clue.text: Thatcher's material sin: ignoring the far left

indicators.note: the far left of a word is its first letter, which is left out here

parts.note: greed is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: A political jibe: Margaret Thatcher's materialism was sinful, unlike the far left.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop G from GREED. 'Thatcher' suggests the prime minister, but means a roofer working with straw; 'material' is a noun, not 'materialistic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried stalks of a waterside grass are a traditional roofing material laid by thatchers.

clue.text: Taps outside when ready

indicators.note: outside means the two tap letters go on either side of the little word

parts.note: taps are marked C and H for cold and hot
as means when, as in as it happened

explanation.surface: Someone notes taps are fitted outside when everything is prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: C and H (the cold and hot taps) go around AS. 'Ready' is the noun, as in British 'readies' for money. Johnny is the theme's country singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready money, or readies, is British slang for banknotes and coins available to spend.

clue.text: Someone needing an Equity card? Stripping works

indicators.note: stripping means taking off the outer layers, the first and last letters

parts.note: a works is a factory

explanation.surface: A striptease performer wondering about union membership.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the outer letters of FACTORY. Equity is the British performers' trade union; its card is needed for stage work.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer on stage or screen traditionally had to hold a union card from Equity to work.

clue.text: Cry about getting an onion?

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for cry is read backwards

parts.note: to blub is to cry or sob, an informal British word

explanation.surface: Tears shed over slicing an onion.
explanation.walkthrough: BLUB is reversed. The question mark warns that an onion is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion is a swollen underground storage organ of a plant, a classic example of the type.

clue.text: 'O' put over entrances to elevator doors done for Otis?

indicators.note: put over means placed around, so the round shape covers the initials

parts.note: the letter O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: entrances to means the first letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: An Otis lift engineer sorting out elevator doors.
explanation.walkthrough: RING (the shape of O) goes around E, D, D, the initials of 'elevator doors done'. Otis is the lift maker but also the soul singer of '(Sittin' On) The Dock of the Bay'.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the soul singer Otis completes the name, just as a lift brand misleads.

clue.text: Ground control building its last shed at 100 mph

indicators.note: its last shed means the building loses its final letter

parts.note: a house is a building
a ton is British slang for 100 miles per hour

explanation.surface: Mission control reporting a building shedding pieces at high speed.
explanation.walkthrough: HOUSE less its last letter, then TON (a hundred mph; 'at' joins). The NASA mission control centre is in this Texas city, as in 'we have a problem'.
explanation.definitionFit: NASA's Johnson Space Center in this Texan city is mission control, addressed by astronauts from orbit.

clue.text: That lady's next in line, not I

indicators.note: not I means the letter I is removed

parts.note: an heir is next in line to inherit

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a woman, not the speaker, is next to inherit.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop I from HEIR.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive feminine pronoun means belonging to that woman, a direct substitute for that lady's.

clue.text: Nurse wraps exercise books for someone who works with joints

indicators.note: wraps means the word for a nurse goes round the other letters

parts.note: a carer looks after the sick, as a nurse does
PE is physical education, exercise
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A nurse covering exercise books, for a physiotherapist perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joints' suggests knees and a physio, but means woodworking joints. Karen and Richard were a famous sibling act of the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodworker fits dovetail and mortise joints together when making furniture and frames.

clue.text: Scots' night spent celebrating in hospital unit

definitions.meaning: 25 January supper honouring Robert, Scotland's national poet, with haggis and verse
a specialist ward treating patients injured by fire or scalding

explanation.surface: A Scottish celebration that ends with someone in hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet's supper night is named after him, and a hospital ward for scald injuries shares the name.
